key_insight: By combining notched and notch-free microbeam bending with phase-field fracture modeling, the study extracts both silica glass toughness (Gc) and ultimate tensile strength (σc) from the same framework.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to characterize brittle glass behavior across both crack-driven failure and strength-limited failure, which is valuable for MEMS, microdevices, and reliability design.
method: Fabricate single-notched and bone-shaped amorphous silica microbeams by FIB milling.
Test microbeams in bending to access fracture-dominated and strength-controlled regimes.
Couple FEA with a phase-field fracture model to identify Gc, KIC, intrinsic length scale, and σc.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantified properties for silica glass: Gc = 5.1 J/m², KIC = 0.61 MPa·m^1/2, lc = 9.1 nm, and σc = 6.8 GPa, with parametric studies on notch geometry and measurement error.
watch_item: Results depend on accurate FIB-defined geometry and dimensional metrology, since notch shape and measurement error can materially affect the inferred toughness.
paper_title: A Combined Microbeam and Phase-Field Approach to Identify the Toughness and Ultimate Strength of Amorphous Silica
